claims.statement: The revised EPBD introduces building renovation passports and a common direction for stronger energy-performance certificates and financing mobilization.
The July 2026 Clean Air programme still requires an energy audit and an energy-performance certificate.
As of July 2026, the Clean Air programme said it was still working with banks on a bank pathway under new cooperation rules.

contrary_evidence: The bank pathway was not yet operating under the new rules in July 2026, so the proposed distribution gate does not yet exist.
Mandatory audits already have established qualified providers; normalization alone may not justify a new intermediary.

economics.acquisition_route: Family-company pilot, accredited energy auditors, municipal operators, and one financing-channel integration
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: a national channel processing 10000 properties yearly at 500 PLN net contribution plus monitoring could support more than 1.2m PLN operating profit; 70% founder ownership and retained cash could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 6-7
economics.founder_time: 3-4 hours/day, with field inspection and regulated audit work performed by qualified partners
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 55-70% after contracted site inspection, auditor review, data hardware, and support
economics.payback: Unvalidated: about 50 completed properties at 1500 PLN contribution each could repay the pilot within 18 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 1500-3000 PLN per property plus 40-80 PLN monthly monitoring, with volume pricing to financiers
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each property has staged payments; lenders and installers can route recurring portfolios and monitoring can renew annually

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Property-performance baselines, contractor outcome data, accepted templates, and channel integration
fingerprint.customer: Banks, retrofit finance providers, municipalities, ESCOs, and quality-focused installers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot through the family installer and energy auditors, then embed with one lender or programme operator
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Standard evidence file, anomaly checks, contractor commissioning pack, and optional metered performance monitoring
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Financier, programme operator, installer, or homeowner pays at audit normalization, approved drawdown, and monitoring renewal
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A property seeks retrofit finance or subsidy payment and needs credible before-and-after evidence

founder_fit: Rewards measurement, anomaly detection, and process automation
Fieldwork can be delegated to qualified auditors
Can start with a small regional validation cohort
risks: Banks and public programmes may build their own evidence workflows
Incorrect assurance could create professional liability
Hardware and site visits can reduce software-like margins

structure.commercial_archetype: Independent measurement-and-verification utility paid per financed property
structure.control_point: A lender- or programme-accepted property evidence record required at approval, drawdown, or warranty review
structure.critical_dependency: At least one bank, subsidy operator, or ESCO must accept the protocol in its funding workflow

thesis: Create an independent evidence record that lenders, subsidy operators, and ESCOs can use at approval and payout for Polish home retrofits: pre-work audit normalization, contractor scope checks, commissioning evidence, and post-work energy monitoring. The business only becomes durable if a financing or subsidy channel adopts its record as a default gate.
title: Renovation Finance Evidence Utility
uncertainties: Polish implementation details for renovation passports
Whether a financier will make third-party evidence a real gate
Measured savings may be too noisy for simple guarantees
